missing: Demonstrate that a vault can reach totalAssets() == 0 and remain staked to the DSS; the PoC should verify the stake after finishRedeem.
Clarify that startRedeem/finishRedeem is the intended withdrawal flow and that completing it does not itself indicate a vulnerability.
reason: The cited code supports the zero-amount revert and the loop can make it block other vault slashes. The PoC does not establish that its zero-asset vault remains in the DSS slashing set after withdrawal. If confirmed, the demonstrated impact is a temporary blockage of slashing, supporting medium severity.

evidence.claim: finalizeSlashing reverts (ZeroAmount) when a vault's totalAssets is 0, blocking slashing of all other vaults in the same request
evidence.support_reason: Vault.slashAssets (Vault.sol:198) computes transferAmount = Math.min(totalAssets(), totalAssetsToSlash); with totalAssets()==0 transferAmount==0, then unconditionally calls handleSlashing (Vault.sol:202). SlashingHandler.handleSlashing reverts on amount==0 (SlashingHandler.sol:53). SlasherLib.finalizeSlashing loops over all vaults (SlasherLib.sol:134-139) with no try/catch, so one zero-asset vault reverts the whole finalize. No check elsewhere prevents a vault from reaching totalAssets==0 (withdrawals via finishRedeem reduce balance; slashAssets caps at totalAssets).
preconditions: DSS requests slashing across multiple vaults of an operator
at least one vault's totalAssets becomes 0 before finalize (full redeem finished, or prior 100% slash by another DSS)
missing_evidence: confirmation that a vault can reach totalAssets==0 while still staked to the DSS (finishRedeem does not unstake from DSS)
note that the PoC's startRedeem/finishRedeem path is the intended withdrawal flow, not a bug itself
